# AI如何帮助NASA在火星、土卫六及其他地方寻找生命

![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/138/1d69be13c7846f9593fca39a35265ec7:ae36aa074d14563fd280a70ab44acf75/titan-nasa.webp)
NASA的卡西尼号探测器拍摄了这张俯瞰土卫六北极的照片 | 图片来源：NASA

随着NASA计划于2028年发射前往土卫六的“蜻蜓”任务以及作为ExoMars计划的一部分，AI将被用于分析样本并做出自主决策。

在她的博士论文《NASA的生命与人工智能：科学家和工程师如何开发工具探索其他世界》中，查尔姆斯理工大学的博士候选人Alicja Ostrowska深入探讨了AI在天体生物学中的应用。

该研究基于在NASA戈达德太空飞行中心进行的实地工作，这里的科学家和工程师正在开发旨在帮助人类在遥远行星和卫星上寻找生物特征或生命迹象的漫游车、机器人和火箭。

## 机器人任务和光谱学

截至2026年，NASA的好奇号和毅力号漫游车仍在红色星球上积极活动，收集样本并向地球发送大量数据。

它们是天体生物学的任务，调查古代生命的迹象——这些迹象可能存在于火星更湿润和温暖的时候。

这两辆漫游车在其“腹部”携带强大的质谱仪，用于通过创建光谱图像来识别样本中的分子，并将这些图像发送回地球供科学家们分析。

另一个特别引起科学家兴趣的遥远天体是土星最大的卫星——土卫六，“这是除地球外唯一一个表面有液态水体的地方”。

唯一的问题是，土卫六及其秘密距离我们15亿公里。

这台上镜的漫游车在第2082个火星日（2018年6月15日）使用火星手持透镜成像仪（MAHLI）在盖尔陨石坑自拍 | 图片来源：NASA

鉴于这一距离，从土卫六传输任何数据到地球需要70-90分钟。

即使如此，科学家们预计一些数据会在传输过程中丢失，正如Alicja解释的那样：“在整个以光速进行的星际旅程中，信号会变得越来越弱，离地球越远就越弱。”

随着其雄心勃勃的“蜻蜓”任务计划于2028年7月发射，预计2034年到达土卫六表面，NASA转向AI来解决数据传输问题。

## 科学自主的AI

对于NASA戈达德太空飞行中心的一群科学家和程序员来说，解决数据传输挑战的方法被称为“科学自主”。

在她的论文中，Alicja将科学自主描述为一种原则，即“科学仪器应自主运行、分析、调整和指导自己”。

“在未来任务中，算法可能会决定宇宙中哪些信息值得了解。”

![Youtube占位符](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/t9G36CDLzIg/hqdefault.jpg)

美国国家标准与技术研究所（NIST）维护权威的质谱参考数据库，而NASA则提供来自哈勃、詹姆斯·韦伯、开普勒、TESS、斯皮策、WISE和钱德拉等任务的大规模公开数据集，这些数据集通过官方存储库如MAST、IRSA、HEASARC和行星数据系统归档，广泛用于机器学习应用。

无人机器人任务，如欧洲航天局的ExoMars罗莎琳德·富兰克林漫游车前往火星和NASA的蜻蜓号前往土卫六，都配备了机载光谱仪来分析样本。ExoMars将数据传回地球进行ML辅助分析，而蜻蜓号将在土卫六上使用AI自主优先处理数据。

Alicja指出：“在戈达德开发的AI将决定哪些质谱图最有趣，以便发送回地球。”

“最终，当NASA的科学家在地球上收到由AI分析的数据时，他们将在计算机屏幕上看到显示的顶级类别，建议哪些最有可能符合样本。”

## 使用AI进行天体生物学的担忧

在这些复杂项目中使用AI的主要问题是“AI的好坏取决于它所学习的数据”。

艺术家对NASA蜻蜓号在土卫六表面的概念图 | 图片来源：NASA

由于我们没有来自土卫六的数据，科学家和程序员将训练这些算法使用所谓的“行星模拟物”的数据——地球上的不同地点用作现场站点。

Alicja指出，这些数据来自“可访问、受欢迎或有声望的研究地点。这是一个例子，说明AI训练的数据偏向于具有吸引力或工业用途的现象，而不是行星科学。”

即使忽略这种偏爱，我们拥有的数据也“严重偏向于地球生命”。

由于某些元素在其他行星上可能干扰实验仪器，结果可能会出现偏差。

作为一种新兴科学，考虑到当前的发现机制，一些科学家认为“天体生物学作为一个整体是一个巨大的类比”。

# How AI Helps NASA Seek Life on Mars, Titan and Beyond
By [Rithula Nisha Ebrahim](https://aimagazine.com/author/rithula-nisha-ebrahim)
January 29, 2026
![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/138/1d69be13c7846f9593fca39a35265ec7:ae36aa074d14563fd280a70ab44acf75/titan-nasa.webp)
NASA's Cassini spacecraft took this image looking down on the north pole of Titan \| Credit: NASA
With NASA's Dragonfly mission to Titan & part of the ExoMars program set to launch in 2028, AI will be used to analyse samples & make autonomous decisions
In her doctoral thesis, _Life and AI at NASA: An Ethnography of How Scientists and Engineers Make Tools to Explore Other Worlds_, Alicja Ostrowska, a doctoral candidate at Chalmers University of Technology, dives deep into the use of AI in astrobiology.
The study is based on fieldwork with scientists and engineers at NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, who are developing the rovers, robots and rockets designed to help humans look for biosignatures, or signs of life, in distant planets and moons.
Alicja Ostrowska, doctoral candidate at Chalmers University of Technology
## Robot missions and spectrometry
As of 2026, NASA’s Curiosity and Perseverance rovers actively roam the red planet, collecting samples and broadcasting vast amounts of data back to Earth.
They are missions in astrobiology, investigating signs of ancient life – which may have existed back when Mars was wetter and warmer.
Both rovers carry powerful mass spectrometers inside their “bellies”, which are used to identify molecules in a sample by creating a spectral image, which they send back to Earth to be analysed by the expert eyes of scientists.
Another distant heavenly body of particular interest to scientists is Titan, Saturn’s largest moon – “the only place beyond Earth with bodies of liquids on its surface”.
The only problem is that Titan and its secrets are 1.5 billion kilometres away.
The photogenic rover created this self-portrait at Gale Crater on Sol 2082 (June 15, 2018) using the Mars Hand Lens Imager or MAHLI \| Credit: NASA
Given this distance, it would take 70-90 minutes for any data from Titan to be transmitted back to Earth.
Even then, scientists expect some data to be lost on the way, as Alicja explains: "Throughout the interstellar journey at the speed of light, the signal becomes weaker and weaker, the farther away the planet is”.
With its ambitious “Dragonfly” mission to explore the surface of Titan set to launch in July 2028, with an expected arrival in 2034, NASA has turned to AI to solve the data-distance problem.
## AI for science autonomy
For a group of scientists and programmers at the [NASA](https://aimagazine.com/news/nasa-taps-planette-for-quantum-weather-prediction-system) Goddard Space Flight Center, the solution to the challenge of data transfer is what is called “science autonomy”.
In her thesis, Alicja describes science autonomy as the principle where “scientific instruments should operate, analyse, tune and direct themselves autonomously”.
“In future missions, algorithms might make decisions about what is worth knowing about the universe.”
![Youtube Placeholder](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/t9G36CDLzIg/hqdefault.jpg)
National institute of standards and technology (NIST) maintains authoritative mass spectrometry reference databases and NASA provides large, publicly accessible datasets from missions such as Hubble, James Webb, Kepler, TESS, Spitzer, WISE and Chandra, archived through official repositories including MAST, IRSA, HEASARC and the Planetary Data System, all of which are widely used in machine-learning applications.
Non-crewed robotic missions such as the European Space Agency's ExoMars Rosalind Franklin rover to Mars and NASA’s Dragonfly to Titan are equipped with onboard spectrometry instruments to analyse samples, with ExoMars sending data back to Earth for ML-assisted analysis, while Dragonfly will use AI to autonomously prioritise and process data on Titan.
“The AI being developed at Goddard will make decisions about which mass spectra are the most interesting to send to Earth,” Alicja notes.
“Ultimately, when NASA scientists on Earth receive the data analysed by AI, they will see it on a computer screen with a display of the top categories, suggesting which are the most likely to fit the sample”.
## Concerns of using AI for astrobiology
The major problem in using AI for these sophisticated projects is that “AI is only as good as the data it learns from”.
Artist's concept of NASA's Dragonfly on the surface of Saturn's moon Titan \| Credit: NASA
Since we do not have any data from Titan, scientists and programmers will be training these algorithms on data from what are called “planet analogs” – different places on Earth which are used as field sites.
Alicja notes that this data comes from places “that are accessible, popular or prestigious to study. This is one example of how the data that AI is trained on, are biased towards phenomena that are charismatic or relevant for industrial purposes, rather than planetary science.”
Even if this favouritism is ignored, the data we have is “biased heavily toward Earth life”.
As certain elements found on other planets could interfere with the instruments used for the experiments, there is a possibility for results to be skewed.
As a science in its infancy, taking the current mechanisms of discovery into account, some scientists say that “astrobiology as a whole is one single, great analogy".

# 马克·扎克伯格与迈向超级人工智能的驱动力
马克·扎克伯格是人工智能领域的重要人物之一，他推动了Meta塑造下一代智能系统的发展。
![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/138/d66e1c8058a992612906e0de6d78c549:83271fe2b84e5be5739f67042bca5685/mark-zuckerberg-meta.webp)
在《AI杂志》2026年全球100位领导者榜单中排名第6位，马克·扎克伯格正在引领Meta的开源模型和超级智能雄心。
## 从Facebook到Meta
马克最初作为Facebook的联合创始人崭露头角，将它从一个学生平台转变为世界上最强大的科技公司之一。
在过去的二十年里，他领导着这个组织——于2021年更名为Meta——经历了数字通信、广告和沉浸式技术的重大转变。
今天，他的注意力已经转向了人工智能，在这一领域，他正带领Meta经历其最具雄心的技术投资和转型期。
他的领导风格结合了长期愿景和快速执行，使Meta能够直接与主要的人工智能玩家如OpenAI、Google和Anthropic竞争。
## 推动Meta的开源人工智能革命
马克在人工智能领域如此有影响力的一个最明显的原因是Meta对开源开发的承诺。
2025年，该公司推出了其Llama大型语言模型（LLM）系列的第四代，引入了Scout和Maverick，并预览了更大的Behemoth。
这些模型设计用于从企业应用到内容创建和多模态处理的各种任务，这意味着它们可以理解和生成文本、图像、视频和音频。
通过公开发布这些模型，Meta将其与那些通常将模型锁定在商业付费墙后的竞争对手区分开来。
马克认为，开放性加速了创新，并确保人工智能工具对全球开发者都是可访问的。
![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/668/25c90e31117d7b9741a66d0a0904ca92:17f86a4b26a38e465b2e593181e15447/work-graphics-2025-08-21t151823-891.jpg)
马克·扎克伯格和Meta正在积极追求人工超级智能
## 构建超级智能并大规模投资
马克还因Meta构建通用人工智能的雄心而成为头条新闻。
Meta的战略包括重大收购和投资，例如以143亿美元收购Scale AI，并将创始人Alexandr Wang纳入高级领导层。
此外，Meta刚刚宣布计划在一年内投入高达1350亿美元用于人工智能基础设施，强化了马克对人工智能将重新定义人们工作和生活方式的信念。
尽管一些高管警告称存在人工智能泡沫，但马克继续采取激进的投资策略，押注人工智能将成为下一个时代的关键技术。
从推进开源多模态模型到招募精英人才并投入数十亿美元建设基础设施，马克·扎克伯格已成为塑造人工智能格局的最有影响力的人物之一。
他的影响力不仅限于Meta，还帮助决定了人工智能如何在全球经济中构建、共享和部署。

# Mark Zuckerberg and the Drive Towards AI Superintelligence
By [Tom Chapman](https://aimagazine.com/author/tom-chapman)
January 29, 2026
![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/138/d66e1c8058a992612906e0de6d78c549:83271fe2b84e5be5739f67042bca5685/mark-zuckerberg-meta.webp)
Mark Zuckerberg, CEO at Meta
Ranked No. 6 in AI Magazine’s Top 100 Leaders 2026 list, Mark Zuckerberg is steering Meta’s open source models and superintelligence ambitions
Mark Zuckerberg has emerged as one of the defining figures in artificial intelligence, driving Meta’s push to shape the next generation of intelligent systems.
Mark has just been ranked No. 6 on [AI Magazine](https://aimagazine.com/)’s list of the Top 100 Leaders 2026, demonstrating his growing impact on the global AI race.
As CEO of [Meta](https://aimagazine.com/company/meta), he has positioned the company at the forefront of open innovation, multimodal AI development and the pursuit of artificial general intelligence (AGI).
_**To read the Top 100 list in full, [click here](https://aimagazine.com/magazine/top-100-ai-leaders-2026).**_
## From Facebook to Meta
Mark first rose to prominence as co-founder of Facebook, transforming it from a student platform into one of the world’s most powerful technology companies.
Over the course of two decades, he has led the organisation – rebranded as Meta in 2021 – through major shifts in digital communication, advertising and immersive technologies.

Today, his attention has turned decisively towards AI, where he is steering Meta through one of its most ambitious periods of technological investment and transformation.
His leadership combines long-term vision with fast execution, enabling Meta to compete directly with major AI players such as [OpenAI](https://aimagazine.com/company/open-ai), [Google](https://aimagazine.com/company/google) and [Anthropic](https://aimagazine.com/company/anthropic).
## Driving Meta’s open source AI revolution
One of the clearest reasons Mark is so influential in AI is Meta’s commitment to open source development.
In 2025, the company launched the [fourth iteration of its Llama large language model (LLM) family](https://aimagazine.com/articles/what-metas-new-ai-models-mean-for-the-global-ai-race), introducing Scout and Maverick, alongside a preview of the much larger Behemoth.
These models are designed for tasks ranging from enterprise applications to content creation and multimodal processing, meaning they can understand and generate across text, images, video and audio.
By releasing them openly, Meta has set itself apart from competitors whose models are often locked behind commercial paywalls.
Mark has argued that openness accelerates innovation and ensures AI tools are accessible to developers worldwide.
![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/668/25c90e31117d7b9741a66d0a0904ca92:17f86a4b26a38e465b2e593181e15447/work-graphics-2025-08-21t151823-891.jpg)
Mark Zuckerberg and Meta are aggressively pursuing artificial superintelligence
## Building superintelligence and investing at scale
Mark has also made headlines through Meta’s ambition to build artificial general intelligence.
Meta’s strategy has included major acquisitions and investments, such as its US$14.3bn stake in Scale AI, bringing founder Alexandr Wang into a senior leadership role.
What's more, Meta has just announced plans to spend up to US$135bn on AI infrastructure in a single year, reinforcing Mark's belief that AI will redefine how people work and live.
Despite warnings from some executives about an AI bubble, Mark continues to take an aggressive investment approach, betting that AI will be the defining technology of the next era.
From advancing open source multimodal models to recruiting elite talent and investing billions into infrastructure, Mark Zuckerberg has become one of the most powerful figures shaping the AI landscape.
His influence stretches beyond Meta, helping determine how AI will be built, shared and deployed across the global economy.
![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/668/0eb72cdffd75de8bb0fe00d0e1ab0d55:755222fcb1157524e7fe335b5773c791/ai-top-100-leaders-out-now-cms.jpg)
The Top 100 AI Leaders 2026 is out now
## The Top 100 AI Leaders 2026
The Top 100 AI Leaders 2026 recognises the individuals driving real-world impact through artificial intelligence, from scaling enterprise adoption to advancing responsible and ethical AI.
Our inaugural leaders list highlights the experts and executives who are shaping how AI is developed, governed and deployed across industries including technology, finance, healthcare, manufacturing and energy.
_**To read the Top 100 list in full, [click here](https://aimagazine.com/magazine/top-100-ai-leaders-2026).**_
